newsitem.title: UK: Europe Iran, Libya dealings slammed by U.S. aide.
newsitem.headline: Europe Iran, Libya dealings slammed by U.S. aide.

text.p: The legislative director for the U.S. senator who sponsored last year's sanctions bill aginst Iran and Libya on Tuesday slammed European Union countries for not supporting the measures.

Gregg Rickman, legislative director for Republican senator Alfonse D'Amato, said European countries by refusing to endorse a secondary boycott on international companies that invest in Iran's oil and gas sector were supporting Iranian sponsored terrorism.
"If our friends in Europe wish to deal with the devil then so be it," Rickman told an oil industry conference in London.
"Europe can either be part of the problem or part of the solution."

President Bill Clinton in 1996 signed the Iran/Libya sanctions bill designed to punish foreign companies which invested in the two countries. The United States already imposed a comprehensive trade ban preventing U.S. companies from dealing with Iran and Libya. Rickman singled out France and Germany in particular as culprits.
"I must say European countries such as Germany and France...have facilitated Iran's aggression,"
He said France had been "over eager in its pursuit of trade" with Iran, while Germany had Teheran let off lightly with cheap loans.
"Europe would rather turn a blind eye than lose business opportunities," he said.
"The supineness of our European allies against Libya and Iran has been painful to watch." he said.

Appearing on the same platform, director of the oil and gas department of the French Ministry of Industry Guy Arlette said that the U.S. sanctions laws "are not in accordance to international law and we are going to react to it, it is underway."
"We certainly do not favour terrorism, there is a dialogue between Europe and Iran in which differences of opinion are discussed in very clear terms and we prefer that," Arlette said.
Rickman said Teheran mounted a direct challenge to U.S. security in its support for terrorist groups.
"Iran's economic enrichment is a threat to the US and the West. Any increase in Iranian and Libyan oil revenues should be seen as a threat to the security of the United States," he said.
Also on the same platform was Hamid Moussavi, director of Naft Iran trading services and international affairs advisor of the National Iranian Oil Company.
"Somehow the U.S. always tries to link terrorism with Iran," he said in the course of a sometimes heated discussion. "In U.S. eyes we are guilty and have to prove we are innocent."
